svg.title: Mrs. K, 74, is day 2 after a laparoscopic hysterectomy and still has an indwelling urinary catheter. Overnight she has become quieter and more tired. Her daughter says she is not herself. She denies chest pain and shortness of breath. Her baseline is alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation.
svg.desc: Sepsis on a medical-surgical floor is recognized in small changes such as new confusion and a fast respiratory rate, treated against the clock, and then judged by lactate and organ function rather than by temperature.
